nodes.text: The method scales as O(d^3) in both FLOP complexity and parameter count as the number d of residual streams increases.
The matrix M satisfies M^T J_d = M J_d = J_d.
mHC-lite defines learned connections as a convex combination of d! permutation matrices, where d is the number of residual streams.
mHC-lite has O(dC · d!) cost and is not tenable when scaling beyond d > 8.
KromHC uses tensor products to train residual connections on a smaller set of exactly double-stochastic matrices, sacrificing expressivity and complete coverage of B_d.
KromHC costs O(d^2 C).
The layer update is x_(l+1) = H_l^res x_l + (H_l^post)^T F(H_l^pre x_l, W_l).
AGM^fwd(H_(l→L)^res) = max_i Σ_j |(H_(l→L)^res)_ij|.
AGM^bwd(H_(l→L)^res) = max_j Σ_i |(H_(l→L)^res)_ij|.
The set contains complex eigenvalues λ for which H^res v = λv with v ≠ 0 and H^res = P_M(⋯).
The set is {e^(i2πj/d′) | j ∈ [1,d′], d′ ≤ d}.
The function Φ_{d,s} maps Q_l to an exactly doubly stochastic matrix H_l^{res} ∈ B_d.
AGM metric is ambiguous in the supplied context; it commonly denotes an arithmetic–geometric-mean-based quantity, but the paper-specific definition is not available.
P_go is ambiguous in the supplied context; it likely denotes the go-mHC parameterization map, but its exact domain, codomain, and construction are not provided.
Spectral reach is the set or region of eigenvalues attainable by matrices produced by a parameterization.
P_M is ambiguous in the supplied context; it likely denotes a parameterization or projection map associated with method M, but no defining construction is provided.
Method M is ambiguous in the supplied context because no method named M or its defining procedure is provided.

An s-orthostochastic matrix is a doubly stochastic matrix obtained from an orthogonal block matrix by taking normalized squared Frobenius norms of its s×s blocks; s=1 gives an ordinary orthostochastic matrix.
mHC is a manifold-constrained hyper-connection method that parameterizes mixing among multiple residual streams under a doubly stochastic constraint.
mHC-lite is a constrained mHC variant whose parameterization remains within the doubly stochastic polytope while retaining broad mixing expressivity.
KromHC is a hyper-connection parameterization that constructs stream-mixing matrices as Kronecker products of smaller doubly stochastic matrices.
go-mHC is a manifold-constrained hyper-connection method that directly parameterizes generalized orthostochastic stream-mixing matrices, with block parameter s controlling expressivity.
H_res is the residual-stream mixing operator or space of possible mixing terms used by a hyper-connection across d residual streams.
d-streams are the d parallel residual streams whose representations are mixed by a hyper-connection matrix.
The spectral hull of a matrix class is the region of the complex plane containing all eigenvalues attainable by matrices in that class.
i_k is the dimension of each base factor in a k-fold Kronecker parameterization; here i_k=2 means the construction uses 2×2 factors.
